paper_metadata.title: Educational History Is an Independent Predictor of Cognitive Deficits and Long-Term Survival in Postacute Patients With Mild to Moderate Ischemic Stroke

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a consecutive sample from a defined geographic area with clear criteria. However, there is a significant selection bias acknowledged by the authors: 11.1% died before the 3-month assessment and 12.8% refused. The resulting cohort is skewed toward mild/moderate strokes, and women are underrepresented compared to regional mortality data, which may distort the relationship between education and survival.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of these, 71 died (11.1%) before the 3-month follow-up, 82 refused (12.8%), and 3 were lost (0.5%) because of undefined causes. Finally, 486 of the living patients were included in the cohort.
items.reasoning: While 486/642 is a decent number, the loss of nearly 25% of the eligible sample before the 'zero time' of the prognostic study (3 months post-stroke) introduces significant selection bias, as noted by the authors regarding stroke severity.
